utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone in this courtroom, and as always, also to those just outside the courtroom, without whose help we couldn't function.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, may I first announce to the parties, as far as Friday is concerned: This Chamber has not the full Friday afternoon available, because we have a Status Conference and an additional initial hearing. But that would not take the whole of the Friday afternoon. So presumably we might be ready with that at 3.15 or 3.30. If it looks as if it would be possible to finish on Friday, the Chamber would very much like to continue the second half of Friday afternoon, and this, of course, asks some arrangements also for you, Mr. Krajisnik, because usually either you arrive for the afternoon or you leave at the end of the morning, in the early afternoon. So care will then be taken that it -- that at least you get something for lunch here. Unless you'd say that's too much for me, I insist on continuing on Monday, then we'll consider that. I'm not saying that we're going to do that, but we'll consider it. But if there's no firm objection from your side, we'll try to finish Friday in the afternoon, if at all needed, because finishing Friday morning would even be better.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no. I will be glad to see us finish this as soon as possible, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik, for your cooperation. Then, Mr. Tieger, if there's nothing else, you may proceed with the examination-in-chief of Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, good morning.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd like to move as quickly and as efficiently as possible through the remaining material and to give you some idea of the pace at which I'd like us to proceed, I hope we can begin addressing, for example, the 16th Assembly Session by the beginning of the third session of today. For that reason, I will only be drawing your attention to a limited number of highlights, those portions of the documents that you've highlighted, and it may not be possible to discuss those highlights in as much detail as you otherwise would. I don't want you to feel rushed, but I would ask you to make your responses as concise as possible, as you explained to the Court why you selected that passage. And I would also note that a number of documents may be -- will be addressed by other witnesses. I'll try to bring those to your attention as they arise. If we could begin, then, at tab 99. The constitutional law for implementing the constitution, I would like to go through the provisions of the constitution relating to the powers of the president, the powers of the Assembly, and so on, as quickly as possible. The Court will have them available to study in more detail if required. Beginning, then, at constitutional law for implementing the constitution, you have highlighted first Article 5, which addresses the election of the first president by the Assembly, and Article 6, which indicates that until the election of the president, the rights and obligations will be carried out by the Council of Ministers. I'll move on to tab 100, the decree on promulgation of the government, unless there are some necessary comments about those provisions.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think they're self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, at tab 100, you've highlighted Article 10, which indicates that the president and the government are responsible to the Assembly, and also Article 15, which indicates that the government is responsible to the Assembly for proposing policies and enforcement of laws.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning back to tab 96, at which we find the decision on proclaiming the constitution, you have highlighted first Article 80, which addresses the role and authority of the president. Article 81 -- and Article 80, I should indicate, is found on page 13, at tab 96. You've also highlighted Article 81, which indicates the president can declare a state of emergency, and in war or imminent threat of war, can pass enactments later to be confirmed by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a particularly important article. It will come into use later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You've also highlighted Article 82, at page 14, which indicates that the president may convene the government and have its state views. And you've highlighted Article 87, which indicates the term of office.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn next to tab 102, the Law on National Defence. I note first that we've already seen the promulgation of government act, which is located at tab 100. With respect to the Law on National Defence, you've highlighted Article 5, which is found on page 2, which indicates that the Assembly shall organise the National Defence. You've also --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I would point out here, buried in that article, there's reference to the president in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the benefit of counsel, we are now at tab 102, Law on National Defence. You've also highlighted Article 6, which indicates that the president shall supervise the Territorial Defence, submit a plan of defence, and issue orders for utilisation of police during war?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you've highlighted Article 39, which indicates that the president shall order deployment of the Territorial Defence in threat of war or other emergencies.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn now to tab 103, which contains the Law on Internal Affairs. You've highlighted Article 25, which appears at page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The binder that I have here, Your Honour, only has number 100, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the original B/C/S, Madam Registrar, we have got a copy as well. Could I have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I see that binder 9 is split up in the B/C/S version, and 9A and 9B, so if Mr. Krajisnik could be provided with 9B now. 9A, I'm sorry. It's 9A. So if 9A, which starts with 101, could be provided to --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, we were not provided with B/C/S versions of I think 102 and 103, and also we don't have a 106, Your Honour, at all, neither English or B/C/S. So that's -- and 105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were these documents on the list provided for Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, in all likelihood, Your Honour, it's just that with the hard copy versions of the ten folders we received, these particular documents were missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say they might have been disclosed, they might have been --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Might have been on the CD, on the exhibit, but they're not actually in the folders that we were supplied with; that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you check on the CD so that Mr. Krajisnik can follow the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No. We just noticed it this morning, unfortunately, Your Honour, that they were missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have understanding, since the hard copies are distributed in a rather late stage, that I do understand that you only noticed this this morning. This, of course, is exactly the reason why the Chamber introduced that list. Whether everything was disclosed and whether it was in both languages, but I have understanding for the specific circumstances at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, we have another technical problem, especially the registrar cannot use LiveNote at this moment on her laptop computer, and she should, because if there's ever any need to make any redaction, she needs a connection with LiveNote. That would take ten minutes. Would these ten minutes not be an excellent time to try to get hold of the B/C/S versions of exactly those exhibits you just mentioned? Perhaps the parties could come together and see what's missing, so that we could then proceed after this ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until -- I can't see the clock, but it will be 25 minutes past 9.00. --- Break taken at 9.15 a.m. --- Upon resuming at 10.02 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not all technical problems have been solved. What we have at this moment, we have LiveNote scrolling on our main screen. Most of us have no LiveNote on their laptop computers, but there are a few laptop computers that do function properly, one of them is the laptop of the registrar, the other one is the laptop of the legal officer of chambers. Whenever a party needs to find the exact wording of what has been said and which does not appear on the screen any more, it's confirmed by the Registry and by our legal officer that they will gladly assist anyone who needs to scroll back. It will be done for them. It will then be read out, if you guide them to the exact place. I think we could try to proceed in this way. It's also a handicap for me, because I'm one of the most enthusiastic users of my laptop. But it's suggested that we continue. I do not see any nodding no by the parties, so I take it that we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, and we hope that everything will be functioning properly again soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can indicate from the Defence perspective, Your Honour, we're happy to continue without the benefit of the laptops, and I can also indicate that Mr. Krajisnik now has the relevant B/C/S documents that were missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least one of the advantages of having a break of almost three quarters of an hour. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We were at tab 103, the Law on Internal Affairs. Mr. Treanor, in that document, you have highlighted Article 25, found at page 5, which indicates that the president shall evaluate the work programme of the National Security Service on the basis of a report from the minister and tell the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'd just like to point out in connection with this article that this law is the law which regulates the affairs of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which has included within it two basic services: The public security service, which is the regular police, and the -- in the previous set-up, what was known as the State Security Service, which was basically an internal security service, largely used to monitor the activities of people that were suspect to the communist regime. That particular branch of the ministry in this document under the RS has now been renamed the National Security Service. So the reference here is to that internal security service, and gives the president of the republic certain special oversight over that particular branch of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You've also highlighted Article 33, found at page 7. The president can activate reserve police in emergencies.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This particular clause is included in a long list of items of the -- duties of the central ministry, as opposed to its regional branches.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning back for a moment to tab 99, which contains the constitutional law for implementing the constitution. You have highlighted Article 3, which indicates until the National Assembly is elected the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina carries out their responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We saw that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Article 5 was highlighted, which indicates until the election of the president, the functions are carried out by the members of the Presidency, elected on 18 October 1990.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This article in the constitutional law basically makes Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Koljevic the acting presidents of the republic, that is, they exercise all the powers that are attributed to the president of the republic in the constitution and the legislation we've just seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, my question indicated that the date was 18 October 1990. The date in the article is 18 November 1990. And you've also highlighted Article 6, which indicates until the election of the government, the rights and obligations will be carried out by the Ministerial Council, or Council of Ministers.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. That's a similar transitional provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to tab 104, the minutes of a March 2nd, 1992 meeting of the Presidency of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But before we leave the package of instruments we've just been considering, I'd just like to point out one facet for the Court. The constitution which was adopted and indeed proclaimed on the 28th of February, according to its terms, comes into effect on that day. However, the law on defence and the law on internal affairs, which were also adopted on that day, according to the terms of those laws, would not come into effect until eight days after they were published in the Official Gazette, and they were not published in the Official Gazette until the 23rd of March. When we get to that point, I will hopefully remind the Court of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Turning now to the meeting of March 2nd, 1992 on the first page, you've highlighted a portion which indicates the attendees from Bosnia and Herzegovina, including Dr. Koljevic, Momcilo Krajisnik, and Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the -- this is a record, a rather lengthy record, of the meeting in Belgrade, the invitation to which we saw yesterday. The meeting was originally scheduled for a particular date and then I think rescheduled to the 28th of February. It did not in fact take place until the 2nd of March, which was a Monday, I believe. As we've seen, certainly the Bosnian Serb leaders were very busy on the 28th of March -- 28th of February, adopting their constitution, and then they went to Banja Luka for the meeting there on the 29th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next two documents that you selected, Mr. Treanor, are found at tabs 105 and 106. The first are headlines from March 6th, 1992. The second is an 11 March joint meeting of the Main Board, Executive Board, and political council. Unless you feel it's necessary to pause and comment on either of those, I would move on to the 10th Assembly Session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as long as the Court has the opportunity to read the highlighted portions, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I can address quickly the highlighted portions of those documents. At tab 105, the March 6th headlines, we see highlighted three portions. The first of which is in the upper part of the page and begins: "That is why it is justified and necessary to consolidate ethnic territories in Bosnia and Herzegovina." That's one sentence. The next highlighted portion begins in the second paragraph: "Mr. Vukic also told the Serbian people not to be fooled by invitations to various peace rallies, which are nothing else but Ramadan gatherings, which irritate Serbs," and continues. That is also one sentence. And finally, a section that is the beginning of another paragraph: "At the end of today's press conference, Radoslav Vukic also reflected on the recent events in Banja Luka radio, stressing that the editorial policy of this media organisation to date has not served sufficiently the interests of the ruling party, and that it should, therefore, be changed as soon as possible."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is apparently a news broadcast which was at least prepared at Banja Luka Radio, containing a summary of a press conference of what is described as the regional board of the Serbian Democratic Party in Banja Luka. Whether it was actually broadcast or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And turning to the 11 March 1992 joint meeting, we see highlighted the heading indicating the date of the meeting and the organs which attended. And then we also see highlighted the second and third paragraphs on the first page, the first of which begins: "It has to be emphasised that in the sphere of entire relations," and the second of which begins: "In the past negotiations an agreement was reached to constitute Bosnia and Herzegovina upon federal principles."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another one of the series of large meetings that I've mentioned too and we've seen records before of such meetings, where different groups of people, representatives from different organs in the party, get together to have a meeting, rather than meeting separately. At this time, the negotiations under international supervision have resumed, and that is reflected in this document, with giving support to the negotiating group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn, then, to tab 107. The 10th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina, held on 11 March 1992, in Sarajevo. Mr. Treanor, I'm going to direct your attention to three highlights that you've provided from that session, but could you first provide us with some backdrop and context to that session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The work of this session was primarily, almost exclusively, to consider a report from the negotiators regarding the negotiations which had resumed in Brussels just a few days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention to the highlight found at page 3 of the English translation and pages 2 to 3 of the B/C/S original. That's a passage of remarks by Dr. Karadzic which are contained in the second paragraph of the English translation and begin: "Fortunately, Europe realised that a conference on Bosnia and Herzegovina was what was needed," and refer to: "A bloody civil war with hundreds of thousands dead and hundreds of destroyed cities, after which we would have the same situation as we have now, with three Bosnias and Herzegovinas, but only after a war and with much less population and cities which would be completely ethnically homogeneous." And the last sentence reads: "For it must be assumed that the forcible and bloody removal of minority peoples from one region to another would be carried out on a large scale in a civil war."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that needs much commentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next highlighted section is found on page 40 of the English translation, pages 57 to 58 of the B/C/S. I'm sorry. Excuse me. Page 38 of the English.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 57 to 58 in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. I think those would be your highlights 12 -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Here we have Mr. Maksimovic speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, the highlighted portions that appear on page 38 are the second full paragraph, or the first two sentences of the second full paragraph of page 38: "Let us say once again and louder than ever that we see no sense in living in a unitary and so-called independent, indivisible BH." And the sentence that follows that. And then beginning three paragraphs thereafter: "Let us therefore openly tell them to rely only on themselves and instruct them to make preparations for all forms of their own defence." The paragraph after that which refers to: "The resolve not to be the servant and slave of Islamic extremists. The paragraph after that, which refers to: "The death of an innocent Serb near our place of worship, which is a horrendous warning of everything that the perfidious advocates of a Muslim BH are capable of doing." And finally the paragraph after that, which indicates: "Let us instruct our people. Let us show it where the danger is coming from," and ends: "Let us call upon it to take an oath that it will never submit to the just revived beys, qadis, agents and other high officials."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Mr. Maksimovic is providing a strong support for the line that the negotiators are following, that is, that there should be separate constituent units in BH. The reference to the death of the innocent Serb is, I believe, a reference to a man who was shot and killed at a Serbian wedding in Sarajevo at the beginning of March, maybe nine or ten days before this, which led to a certain -- a strong reaction on the part of the Serbs with barricades being erected and that sort of thing, the city being blockaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the reference to beys, qadis, agents and other high officials?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the names of -- titles of various Ottoman officials. This is again a reference of the type we've seen before, to the Ottoman regime of the nineteenth century.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to page 52 of the English, pages 79 through 80 of the B/C/S. I believe those are your highlighted 17 or 18, 17 and 18, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we have Mr. Ostojic, who we've met many times before, speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And do the highlighted passages refer to statements that were prepared to be sent to international parties?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that first portion we see a reference to the 64 per cent of the territory that the Bosnian Serb leadership claims is controlled or settled by Serbs. We've seen that figure before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the highlighted portion is the second paragraph of page 52, beginning: "First, the Serbian people in BH accounts for about 35 per cent of the total population and is settled on cca. 64 per cent of the territory." The last sentence is: "Any unitary arrangement of BH, and especially recognition of the independence of such a state of BH before the three ethnic communities reach agreement may lead to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. interethnic conflicts with disastrous consequences."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an important statement to remember in view of later developments, which we will shortly see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the second highlight is the second-to-last paragraph of that page, which begins: "If we bear in mind the fact that over the past two centuries," and concludes with: "The concern over the inauguration of an independent BH, find ourselves enjoying the status of a national minority which would in a fundamentalist Islamic BH, which it would soon become, call in question the existence of an entire people."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And these two passages are extracts from a draft communique which Mr. Ostojic says has been prepared to send to various states which he identifies as the victor states in the Second World War, Russia, Britain, France, and the USA.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document found at tab 108 is contained in binder 10. Mr. Treanor, I'm going to call your attention to the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'd like to draw your attention to the document contained at tab 108, the 13 March 1992 letter to all municipal boards from the Executive Board. You've highlighted a portion of that document. The first sentence of its substantive contents indicating: "In accordance with the stance adopted you are required to assess the possibility of establishing a Serbian municipality in the area of your activity."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This letter from Rajko Dukic apparently refers to the instruction which had been given on the 19th of December, 1991, regarding the establishment of Serbian municipalities. It appears to represent a reminder and certainly a request for information in that area. The main concern would have been with the so-called Variant B municipalities, although this document is addressed to all municipal boards of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn, then, to the 11th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina, held on 18 March 1992 and contained at tab 109. Mr. Treanor, I'm going to direct your attention to about five of the highlighted portions you selected, but again, before I do that, if you could provide the Chamber with the appropriate backdrop or context to this session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this session is another session that has been called basically to hear a report about the continuing negotiations which have just reached another high point. On the 18th of March, a document was agreed to by the parties. I'm not sure whether that took place before or after this session. In any case, I don't think that's particularly important for understanding this session, since the main outlines were certainly clear already, the main outlines of that document, since discussions had been going on for some time, having resumed in Brussels earlier in the month, as we've seen, and continuing in Sarajevo on the 18th of March, a document was agreed to in Sarajevo, which is a statement of principles for the new constitutional arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina. And the salient points I will indicate in the area that is of most concern to the developments taking place in most relevance, that is, the establishment of constituent units and their boundaries. That document states at the very beginning that Bosnia and Herzegovina would be a state composed of three constituent units based on national principles, and taking into account economic, geographic, and other criteria. And it goes on toward the end of the document to discuss the definition of the constituent units, saying that: "A working group will be established in order to define the territory of the constituent units, based on national principles and taking into account economic, geographical and other criteria. A map based on the national, absolute, or relative majority in each municipality will be the basis of work in the working group and will be subject only to amendments justified by the above-mentioned criteria. A copy is annexed to this statement." Now, this paper, as it states at the very end of it, was only to be the basis for further negotiations. However, it was again seen by the Bosnian Serb delegation as being a great advance. It contained the concession that Izetbegovic, I think, had been looking for, that is, that among the criterion for establishing the units would not only be national but include other factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to one of the sections you've highlighted, found at page 12 of the English and page 16 of the B/C/S, which is a passage from remarks by Mr. Krajisnik. And the portions that you have highlighted are found in the last two paragraphs at the bottom of the page, the first of which is: "I think the problem is that they want Bosnia and Herzegovina to be internationally recognised at any cost. They want it to be a state." And the second of which begins, although it continues on to the next page: "In this respect, it would be good if we could do one thing for strategic reasons: If we could start implementing what we have agreed upon, the ethnic division on the ground." And it concludes on the next page in English with the end of that sentence, which is simply the first four words of that page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is another expression of the desirability of getting the Bosnian Serb Republic up and running as soon as possible, certainly before any international recognition may occur.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to the highlighted portion found at page 31 of the English, page 45 of the B/C/S. Again, these are remarks by Mr. Krajisnik that begin -- the highlighted portion begins toward the bottom of the page, immediately after the indication that the presiding Momcilo Krajisnik is speaking, and begins: "Mr. Kerovic we shall have our own assembly, our own government. We have not had it before. We shall have our own constitution and laws." That highlighted portion continues on to the next page, I believe, with the first four short paragraphs, bulleted paragraphs of that page, and then a final sentence in conclusion -- I think we've lost that on the screen at the moment. The last sentence reads: "I have summed up this as a proposal of conclusions."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Mr. Krajisnik is assuring the delegates that the course of the negotiations is going according to what they had all agreed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the last --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then he returns to the necessity for taking over actual power and the establishment of authority in the republic. As I indicated, the instruments which would have actually gotten the various organs in operation had not come into effect yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that is reflected in the last bulleted point: "A proposal for the takeover of actual power and establishment of authority in a republic of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall be prepared for the next session."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 38 of the English translation, page 54 of the B/C/S. The highlighted portion contains the final paragraph of remarks by Mr. Vjestica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who was a deputy from Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And it reads: "Mr. President, I think that you have to give us an order, that after the next assembly, you should order this, that we arrange it for the areas where it has not been done and to implement this: That the Serbs should occupy their territories so that no other forces could enter them. Thank you." And then the -- and then applause is indicated.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, the advocacy of the idea of actually establishing control in the areas that would form part of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to page 42 of the English, page 60 of the B/C/S. There are a number of highlights, but I'd simply like to draw your attention to the highlight at the top of the page, the speaker is indicated as Dr. Karadzic. The highlighted portion is the second paragraph, which begins: "What we have here is a process." And concludes: "We have entered into this process with our strategic goals and we are accomplishing them stage by stage."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again we have a reference to the idea of attaining the goals that they are all striving for, step by step, and that the present negotiations are an important step in the direction toward the final goal. They do not reach the final goal, but that is still in sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn next, then, to page 45, highlight 14, which is found at page 66 of the B/C/S, the comments by Mr. Krajisnik which appear in the bottom half of the page and begin: "I have realised that responsible government should be established in Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina." And then a number of bulleted points, including: "To find the mechanisms for implementing the BH Constitution, urgently form MUP, National Defence; money transfer systems; take the Serbian territories." And continues on to the next page with approximately -- with - not approximately - with six bulleted points, ending with: "That the personnel committee of the Assembly nominates the prime minister designate and some of the ministers."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again the idea of moving on to actually activating the Serbian Republic. Before we move on, perhaps I should have mentioned, before we considered this session, and within the framework of the negotiations, that certainly no later than the 2nd of March, during the meeting in Belgrade, it was made clear to the Bosnian Serb leaders by high officials of the SFRY that it would not be possible at that time for the new constitution which was being prepared for the SFRY, the constitution of what became the FRY, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and proclaimed on the 27th of April, I believe, that it would not be possible in that constitution and in the course of the adoption of that constitution to include the Bosnian Serb entity, or indeed the Croatian Serb entities, within that new state, for various legal and technical reasons. However, receiving the assurance that that would be possible at a later date. This was rather disappointing for the Bosnian Serb representatives to hear, but it certainly made clear to them that they had to, I think, persist in their efforts to form their own entity within Bosnia, so that it would exist to later be able to unite with the other Serbian entities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next document you've selected is found at tab 110. It is a 20 March 1991 [sic] report, or conclusions, from the estimation of the situation in the area of the BH Republic. This is a document which the Court has previously seen, and for that reason, I would like only to direct your attention to one portion of that document, found at page 4. You've highlighted a portion there which reads: "Second, Serb people determine themselves for Yugoslavia and if it is impossible, then only a confederate Bosnia and Herzegovina comes into consideration. Simply, the third variant does not exist. The leadership of Serb people and Serbs as a whole are ready for the war if the confederate Bosnia and Herzegovina is not going to be accepted."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've just gotten that on the screen. This is an evaluation by the JNA's 2nd Military District, which was headquartered in Sarajevo, of the situation there. The command of the 2nd Military District was in contact with the Bosnian Serb leaders.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the benefit of the record, it comes up on the screen as March 1991. On page 21. And the date of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. report appears to be 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Also from a chronological order, I would not expect us to jump back to 1991. The letter is of the 20th of March and the report is of March 1992. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next document you've selected, Mr. Treanor, is found at tab 111. It is an entry from the Grkovic diary of 23 March 1992, which is found at page 126. The portion you've highlighted is contained at the top, indicating a meeting at 1700 with the Main Board and Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the topic of conversation is indicated as the delineation of -- in the original it says of Serbian BH. This is the only indication we have of this meeting. I would remind the Court at this point, the 23rd of March, that on this day, the Official Gazette published the Law on Defence and the Law on Internal Affairs. According to their terms, it will come into operation eight days later. So at this time, it was obviously foreseen by the Bosnian Serb leaders that their republic would become functional on the 31st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is contained in binder 11 and found at tab 112. That is a 23 March 1992 strictly confidential letter to all presidents of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a letter signed by Dr. Karadzic, as president of the SDS, sent to all presidents of municipalities, presumably Serbian municipalities, informing them of the formation of a republic operation centre and requesting them to make sure that their own information centres, municipal information centres and regional information centres are operational and in contact with the republic centre. I could mention at this point, although the timing is a little bit unclear to me precisely, but certainly about this time - and they were probably quite likely had got some inkling already - that the HDZ and the SDA were about to back off of the 18 March Sarajevo agreement. This happened 23rd, 24th, 25th of March, in that time period. They expressed their dissatisfaction with using the existing municipalities, on the one hand, and with the idea of ethnically based constituent units, on the other. So, once again, the agreement which the Bosnian Serb leaders thought had been reached has fallen through, and to emphasise again, that agreement was merely an agreement on the basis of further negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention next, then, to the next document you selected, which is found at tab 113, and that's the 24 March 1992, 12th Session of the Serbian Assembly.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this session had on its agenda the consideration of further legislation to establish the proper legal framework for the operation of the organs of the Serbian Republic, which as we have seen was two of the most important organs of which were to come into operation on the -- at the end of March. So they met to complete the legislative agenda that they did not complete at the end of February, and they've also met to replace the Council of Ministers with a new government, and in this particular session, to choose a prime minister designate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention to a highlighted portion found at page 14 of the English, page 24 of the B/C/S. The highlighted portion reflects remarks by Dr. Karadzic, toward the bottom of that page, that begin immediately after he is identified as the speaker, beginning: "I quite agree that it is necessary to be very cautious when assigning certain competencies," and then continuing to discuss the composition of the council and the kind of information with which it must deal and the circumstances under which that kind of information can be discussed.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, here what is being referred to is the establishment among the various organs of the new republic, of a National Security Council. This is a matter which the council -- the Ministerial Council have been asked to look into way back in January to draft some proposals. It does not come up in the documentation again until this particular point in time. And there was some discussion in the Assembly as to what exactly the powers of this National Security Council were going to be, would it be an executive organ or merely an advisory organ to the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next clip I'd like to direct your attention to is found at page 18 of the English, page 30 of the B/C/S. And it's the second full paragraph of that page, in which it is stated: "Now in the next month or two everything will be resolved. We shall either achieve our goal or fall apart. There is no other option. We will either fall apart 100 per cent or would finally achieve our goal."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Dr. Karadzic continuing to speak. And you'll see in the next paragraph the reference to promulgating the constitution at the next session, which I think we'll be seeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next -- excuse me. If we could turn next to a highlighted portion found at page 21 of the English and pages 37 and 38, I believe, of the B/C/S, probably on 38. If I could direct your attention in particular to a portion found on the next page, at 22 two portions highlighted there. The first is the second full paragraph of that page, which begins: "Second, it does not suit us at this moment that a National Guard be established. The JNA is much better." And continues on to the end of the paragraph. And then the paragraph that begins: "You can be sure that numbers the police are quite sufficient [sic]." And continues on to discuss that: "At a desired moment, and this will be very soon, we can form whatever we want. There are reasons why this could happen in two to three days." Indicates that at that moment all the Serbian municipalities, both the old ones and newly established ones, would literally assume control of the entire territory of the municipality concerned." It indicates further that: "At a given moment in the next three or four days there will be a method used and you will be able to apply it in the municipalities you represent. How to separate the police force, take the resources," and so on. And it ends with the sentence: "I think that we shall hear about it today in the form of instructions at the Deputies' Club."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Dr. Karadzic is addressing himself to a proposal for the establishment of a -- some sort of National Guard which would be something akin to an army of the Bosnian Serb Republic. He's indicating that this really isn't necessary at this point. The republic, of course, is, in their view, at least, still part of Yugoslavia. Therefore, they have the JNA to cooperate with them. Now, the Territorial Defence, which in many areas they had control of, if it were mobilised, would, in many cases, be operating with the JNA, so therefore, they would be under direct JNA command; hence, I think, the desire of some deputies to form a National Guard which would be directly under the command of the republic leadership. And Dr. Karadzic assures them that they do have the police as well, which is under their control, and that should be perfectly adequate, from their point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention to a highlighted portion found at page 24 of the English, page 11 of the B/C/S. That is a highlighted portion in which Professor Plavsic speaks, and the highlighted portion is comprised of the first two sentences of her remarks, indicating that: "Pursuant to Article 80 of the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the President of the Republic wishes to propose to the National Assembly of the Serbian People a candidate for the premier designate." And then ending: "After consultations between the Presidency of the republic and the personnel commission, we propose that Dr. Branko Djeric for the above position," followed by applause.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see Mrs. Plavsic exercising one of the functions of the president of the republic as specified in the constitution, that is, to name a candidate for the position of president of the government, that is, prime minister. Here she does that, and Dr. Branko Djeric, who is referred to, was a member of the previous Council of Ministers and had been an official previously in the BH government as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, the next document you've selected, Mr. Treanor, is found at tab 114. It is the 13th Session of the Serbian Assembly, held on the same day, 24 March 1992.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the main business of this session was basically to elect -- formally elect the president of the government and some of the ministers. In fact, they apparently had a separate session to do that only a few minutes after the end of the previous session, probably to observe a formality that the designation of the prime minister designate, the selection of the prime minister designate, should happen at one session and then that he should have time to form a government, and then be formally elected by the Assembly at a following session. So this session is mercifully brief, with that being the main item on the agenda. They also considered issuing a statement in connection with the recognition of BH as an independent state, which they had apparently reason to believe at this point may be imminent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I may just direct your attention to two highlighted portions, the first of which is found at page 12 of the English, page 9 of the B/C/S. These are remarks by Mr. Vjestica.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, he's a deputy from Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the highlighted portion, which begins immediately after he's identified as the speaker, begins: "I have not written any conclusion." And then goes on to the end of the page: "To urge the adoption of a conclusion instructing the president of the government to prepare by Friday an operational plan for assuming power." And then continues on to the next page, to the end of his remarks. The last sentence of which reads: "This should be simultaneously effected in all municipalities where we already have Serbian authorities and in those municipalities where we have only recently established Serbian municipalities."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, here again we see an expression of the desire to get moving with the establishment and starting the functioning of the Serbian Republic, and the reference at the end to the recently established Serbian municipalities should be clear by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And on that same page, you've highlighted the remarks of Professor Djeric, which begin: "The government will have the duty to draw up an operational plan and to submit it for adoption," and concludes: "Please do not take things in your own hands. You will receive your instructions and you will proceed as instructed," followed by applause.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, here we see Mr. Djeric giving assurances to the deputies that they will receive instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next document you've selected, Mr. Treanor, is found at tab 115, is a session of the Serbian Assembly three days later on 27 March 1992, the 14th Session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Tieger, may I just raise a practical issue. Our programme is a bit disturbed this morning, through the technical problems. I am not fully aware on whether the interpreters could take a break when we had a pause. As far as the tapes are concerned, but of course, the hardware is always of less importance than the human resources, as far as the tapes are concerned, we could continue until 11.45, have then a half an hour break, which is a bit more than usual, and then have a second session from 12.15 to a quarter to 2.00. That would mean that after we started for approximately 15 minutes in the beginning, that we would have two full sessions of one hour and a half, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with a half-hour break in between. But I do not know, because I do not know what freedom the interpreters had to leave when we were on standby whether this would also suit the interpreters. Because I'm aware of the fatiguing character of their job. So I'd like to hear from the booth whether it would be possible to go on for another 40 minutes, then have a half an hour break and then have one hour and a half --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for your cooperation. It's confirmed to me that we can proceed this way. So, Mr. Tieger, please keep in mind that we'll stop at a quarter to 12.00 and then have a half-hour break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, we had just turned to the 14th Assembly Session. If you could provide us, please, with the background to that session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this session has as its primary business what it describes as - and I'm not sure how it's translated - the -- but I would say the ceremonial proclamation of the constitution. This was foreshadowed in a document we saw today, and I believe it was also made reference to in the session of the 15th of February. That is, even at that time, in February, the leadership foresaw a gradual process of the introduction of a constitution, first it being adopted by the Assembly, as it was on the 28th of February, and then its formal proclamation at a suitable time. The time had obviously now arrived, this being the 27th of March. Again, to remind the Court: The international negotiations by this time had again returned to square one, if you will. They had fallen through. The Bosnian Serb leaders seemed apprehensive that this would in fact lead to international recognition of BH as an independent state. Before the desired transformation, desired by them, had taken place, we have already seen that they started the appropriate procedure for activating, for instance, their Ministry of Internal Affairs by the end of the month, the start of that process already on the 23rd of March, and so here on the 27th, they are now formally proclaiming their constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention, Mr. Treanor, to a highlighted portion found at page 23 of the English, pages 30 through 31 of the B/C/S, highlighted remarks by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to this particular document, I'm given to understand that there may be a difference between the English version and the B/C/S version, in that the English version is transcript and the B/C/S version, I think, is stenographic record, apparently, according to my case manager. That's her recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see in the original, Mr. Tieger, the word "stenogramme," and in the translation, we see "transcript." This is different from what we saw before, because I think there was some reference to an audiotape or something like that. Transcript does not necessarily conflict with stenogramme, but at least it's not the same indication. Could you ask the witness to clarify the issue, or could you clarify it yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, we can certainly do both, Your Honour. First I would say that we went -- last night we went through all of the assembly sessions with just this issue in mind and had them checked by B/C/S speakers. I accept the possibility of human error, but we tried to eliminate that to the extent possible. But perhaps we can triple-check now through the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what I have before me is certainly described as being a stenogramme. The record of this session is a little confusing in itself, in that the stenogramme makes reference to seeing an attachment which is a -- in certain respects, it's certainly numbered -- the pagination begins at 1 -- in certain respects a separate document, which represents the introductory remarks by Mr. Krajisnik. But the main document is certainly described as being a stenogramme.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, also with respect to the transcript, stenographic distinction, I note that on the previous occasion the English translation was rendered very clearly, as you noted, as tape-recording. It certainly seems to suggest that the transcript is an indication that the document is a reflection of the verbatim record of that session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Yes. First of all, we find in the English version, after the cover page, not the handwritten cover page, but the typewritten cover page, I noted that sometimes we find a translation of the handwritten cover page as well. Here we do not, as we also did not in 114 and 113. But I think that should not be the main problem. But after the cover page, we find a few pages in English. As a matter of fact, these are the pages 2 up until 6, starting with: "Ladies and gentlemen, dear brothers and sisters, honoured guests, there are joyous but also difficult moments." And that continues in English up until page 6. And then on page 7, it seems that the minutes of the meeting start, which is the -- in the B/C/S original, the page immediately following the cover page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is the introductory speech by Mr. Krajisnik, which, in some copies of this document, has been inserted between the cover page and the beginning of the stenogramme proper, instead of being put at the end of the document. Within the stenogramme, you will see, in the original, it's in rather large letters - It should be on page 1 or 2 of the translation - "see the attachment." It's under Arabic number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see there also that he reads his address, "See attachment." But would it then not be proper to -- not only to attach the English text of the attachment, but -- in the B/C/S version, also the B/C/S text of this attachment, which, by going through it very quickly, I do not find. Will there be any questions in respect of these introductory speech?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there won't be. And if I could address for a moment--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- very quickly the stenogramme/transcript issue. I'm looking at two pages here which are clearly, at least from my very simplistic and elementary knowledge of B/C/S, the same two pages, and I can tell that from the format and the order in which the words appear, and I simply note that in the B/C/S it says "stenogramme" and goes on to say: "14th Session of the Assembly," and that is rendered in the English, again, which appears to be the identical page, as "transcript." So on that basis, among others, I would say that the distinction previously noted between a tape and a stenogramme does not exist here. This is simply a choice of words for -- to represent the same thing, that is, the stenographic transcript of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't verify it. First of all, I'd like to instruct the Prosecution to attach the B/C/S version of the introductory speech to the tab 115, and I would invite the Defence to further see whether there's any difference in text. If there is, the Chamber would like to be informed. If there is not, it might be just a matter of translation of the word "stenogramme" into "transcript," where you would expect "stenogramme."

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour. We'll be attending to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if I can direct your attention to the highlighted portion on page 23. It is three paragraphs, beginning: "They can attempt to intimidate the Serbs here." The next paragraph, which begins: "We know that our people have armed themselves." And the last paragraph, which begins: "When you return to your municipalities, especially the newly formed municipalities, I ask you to do what you are required and entitled to do under the law." And then it concludes: "The moment you arrive in your municipalities, you must urgently establish Crisis Staffs." And then continues.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is Dr. Karadzic speaking, giving some instructions to the assembled deputies as to what they should now do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the only other highlighted portion of that session, to which I'd like to draw your attention, is page 24 of the English, page 31 of the B/C/S, and in particular, the first highlighted passage they top of the page, which is the first full paragraph, which begins: "A war in Bosnia and Herzegovina will not solve anything. If it breaks out, you will get the plans." And then continues with Dr. Karadzic urging the immediate organisation of people within Territorial Defence units which must be done throughout the areas.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, addressing the next steps to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention next, then, to the document found at tab 116, the decision to set up the National Security Council. And I note for the record that most of the first page is highlighted. That includes paragraphs which are enumerated 1, 2, and 3, in their entirety.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This decision was again considered at this session and adopted. We -- this is the only text of the decision that we have. It is, unfortunately, not a signed copy and it bears no number. It is evident from the record of the session that a decision was in fact adopted. The decision was not published in the Official Gazette. There is, however, an entry in the log of the Assembly, under number 120/02 of such a decision. Whether the text we have here is precisely as it was adopted, we, therefore, unfortunately, do not know. I would point out that in I, the National Security Council is described as an advisory organ of the Assembly. This certainly reflects the concern expressed by some of the deputies that the Assembly might lose some of its authority to this particular body. II indicates the types of matters the council would deal with, specifying that it would be responsible for its work to the Assembly. And then Article 3 discusses the composition of the National Security Council. The Court will note that the presidents of the republic is by virtue of his office the president of the council, and that the president of the Assembly, among others, is by virtue of his office also a member of the council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, you noted Article 1, which refers to the National Security Council as an advisory body. Will we be seeing examples of how the National Security Council actually functioned in upcoming documents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we will, indeed, which are a little bit at variance with what we see here, in more than one respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have one additional question. Is it right to understand Article 6 to mean that the decision will become effective even if not published in the Official Gazette, although there is an instruction to publish it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If I can -- yes, it separates the two things. This is rather unusual wording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I see that in the translation, the brackets -- the quote is missing, but that, I take it, is not a very Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. important issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's -- those are certainly -- simply around the title of the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 117, the document of 31 March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I note that this is a document which will be addressed by at least one other, if not more, witnesses, so I would invite you to be brief in providing the Court an indication of its significance. I should also note that highlighted portion of that document appears in the first lengthy paragraph, beginning: "At its meeting held on 27 March 1992, the Assembly of Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina," et cetera, and concluding with the sentence: "In that respect, it passed a Law on Internal Affairs, which shall be uniformly applied on the territory of the Republic of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina as of 1 April 1992 and appointed Mico Stanisic, until now an advisor in the BH MUP, as minister."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this document simply reflects what I referred to earlier, that is, the activation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs eight days after the publication of the Law on Internal Affairs. Here the date is given for the activation as 1 April rather than 31 March, and also reflects the fact that Mr. Mico Stanisic had been chosen as minister of internal affairs, Mr. Djeric, by the way, also having been confirmed by the Assembly as president of the government on the 24th, as I think we've seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next document found at tab 118 is an April 4, 1992 public announcement by Dr. Karadzic. For the record, you have highlighted the last paragraph of that document, which begins: "If, however, the Territorial Defence, civilian defence, and reserve police were to respond to the invitation of the Presidency, the Serb Council for National Defence instructs that its Crisis Staffs be activated in such areas," and continues on to the end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this document is, first of all, a reflection of the fact that the Bosnian Presidency met on the 4th of April, with the participation of the Bosnian Serb members, and decided on a mobilisation of the Territorial Defence. This document represents a response to that. The other interesting facet that I would call attention to is the fact that it's signed by Dr. Karadzic, as president of the National Security Council. As we saw in the text of the decision that we have, the president of the council was to be the president of the republic. There was no president of the republic, but there were two acting presidents. Why one of them was -- is not signing this as president of the council but Dr. Karadzic is, I don't know, but it's evident from this and later documents that we'll see that Dr. Karadzic was in fact the president of the National Security Council, this being the -- one of the first official positions that he -- other than the negotiator, that we've seen, that he occupies in the Bosnian Serb Republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one clarification. This document, at least in English, says the Serb Council for National Defence. At the same time, we see in the translation of the decision establishing a council for national security. That's the unsigned decision of which you do not know whether it was ever adopted, at least in the form as we find it here. Is there any difference in Council for National Security and Council for National Defence or is that the same in your --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the decision and in the letterhead of this document, the same name is given, which could be translated as "National Security Council" or "Council for National Security." The word is certainly "security," however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it also that the letterhead, as far as I can follow it, gives exactly the same title and is there translated by "National Security Council"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The title --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas in the text of the letter, where it seems that exactly the same words are used, it's translated by "Council for National Defence." Is the wording in the original the same, the letterhead and what I would say the fourth line from the bottom in the original, and also the fifth line from the bottom in the English translation, where it says: "The Serb Council for National Defence."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is the same expression everywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But translated in different ways.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Council For national Security or National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also used in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Treanor, earlier you had mentioned Article 1 of the establishment of the National Security Council and the reference to an advisory body, and then you indicated that we would see documents at variance with that. Here we see the National Security Council instructing Crisis Staffs to be activated. Is that significant in connection with your earlier remarks?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Thank you for reminding me of that. Not only do we see Dr. Karadzic appearing as president of the council, but we see the council - and this is the first document that we have relating to the activities of this body - we see the council acting as an executive organ rather than simply an advisory organ to the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document is found in the intercept binder at tab 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was a brief clip, Mr. Treanor. If you could explain its selection to us, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is in relation to the document that we just considered and the surrounding events. I'll start by observing, however, that it's rather interesting that Mr. Koljevic, who is a member of the Presidency and is one of the acting republics now of the -- acting presidents of the Serbian Republic, refers to Mr. Krajisnik as "Mr. President," and he is, of course, the president of the Assembly, whereas Mr. Krajisnik addresses Mr. Koljevic as "Nikola." On the 4th April, as I mentioned, the Bosnian Presidency, that is, the Presidency of the -- what's still called the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina met at 2.00 in the afternoon. After that session, there were some -- and the mobilisation was decided there. After that session there were some telephone consultations among Dr. Karadzic, Mr. Koljevic, at least, and Mr. Krajisnik, and they arranged to have a meeting at 7.00 in the afternoon -- 7.00 in the evening. It appears to me quite likely that the document we considered just before this, that is, the communique for the public, came out of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could just, I'm sorry, round that off. Which would, in effect, have been a meeting of the National Security Council. We certainly at least have three of its most prominent members mentioned in these conversations. Who else was going to be at that meeting precisely, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused about your remarks in respect of the use of the word "president." In the English translation, I find several times the word "speaker," both used by Biljana Plavsic and by Nikola Koljevic. If I look at the original in B/C/S, it seems that -- and of course, I -- it says something, "predsjednik." Is that what you referred to as "president," or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is -- we render that as "president." It's the same word used for the heads of various organs and bodies in B/C/S, and therefore, I always try to render it as "president," simply to indicate that it is the same word being used everywhere. This is perhaps a confusing facet of their political terminology, but in fact you do have a president of the Assembly, a president of the government, and a president of the Presidency, or a president of the Republic. It's all the same word. The translator here obviously used the word "speaker" as indicating in many countries the title for the presiding officer of a national assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just put this question to you because since your observation was only understandable if looking at the original, rather than to the English translation, which does not give any clue for understanding your observation. But now it's clear to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I wanted to direct your attention to the next document you've selected, found at tab 119, a Radio Beograd network report regarding the proclamations of independence. On that document, you've highlighted the first paragraph, which reads: "In Banja Luka early this morning, the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina proclaimed the independence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which can join a union with other entities in Yugoslavia." And then continues with one more sentence, indicating that the Assembly was informed that Dr. Plavsic and Professor Koljevic had resigned as members of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Presidency.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And I have to remark that this is virtually the only record, if you will, that we have of this session. We do not possess any stenographic notes or minutes, let alone transcript of a tape-recording of this session. But from this and other information, it appears that such a session did take place. The previous session, as we saw, was numbered the 14th Session, and the next session that we have a record of was the 16 Session. So this is presumably the 15th Session, which took the step of proclaiming independence. At this point in time, the international recognition of what was still the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was under way, I believe it was on the 6th of April that the EC recognised the independence of the republic, and I believe it was the 7th that the United States did. They apparently decided that this was an appropriate time to take yet another step of, as it's put here, proclaiming independence. Now, if the Court will remember, according to their constitution, this republic was to be a part of the Federal State of Yugoslavia and not an independent state. However, they had been informed in Belgrade that it would not be possible, in fact, for the authorities of the Yugoslav state to implement that on their part at that particular time, a time during which they were preparing a new constitution for that state. So they have chosen the course of action in this situation to proclaim themselves an independent state.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to tab 120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question. This broadcast report says that Mr. Milovan Milanovic was the chairman of last night's session of the Assembly. Could that give -- have you any information about why it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was Mr. Milanovic and, for example, not Mr. Krajisnik that chaired this Assembly meeting, and whether it -- whether there's any information if he didn't chair it, whether he was present or whether he was elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at this time, Your Honour. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As I indicated earlier, if we could turn to tab 120, the minutes of a joint meeting of the National Security Council and the Government of the Serbian Republic held on 15 April 1992. And on the first page of that document, you've highlighted two portions, the first which indicates those present, including Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Koljevic, Mr. Krajisnik, Dr. Djeric, and so on. And the second highlight which appears in the last paragraph of the document, under item 3, decisions and conclusions: "Reviewing the security situation in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, it was assessed that the conditions had been met to propose that the Presidency of the Republic declare a state of imminent threat of war."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the record -- the first record that we have of a session of the National Security Council proper. As the Court can see, it was a joint session with the government. The government itself was still in process of formation. That is, not all the ministers had been appointed. However, several of the ministers were there, including Colonel Subotic, who was the minister of defence, and Mr. Stanisic, who was the minister of internal affairs. These minutes do indicate again Dr. Karadzic as the president of the council. The portion highlighted at the bottom of the page is interesting in that it indicates a discussion that took place which resulted in a perception that the declaration of an imminent threat of war was necessary, and specified that this be proposed to the Presidency of the Republic, that is, the acting presidents. Now, the acting presidents should have been, one would have thought, one of them would have been the president of the council, but was not. On the other hand, it was certainly the acting presidents, assuming -- performing the functions of the president of the republic that had to sign the decisions that were taken in order that they be implemented and published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Quickly in the remaining time direct your attention to the remaining highlighted portion of this document. And that's a continuation of what we saw on the previous page, the first sentence of the second page, and then the fourth and fifth sentence of page 2: "Decision on the appointment of the acting commander of the Territorial Defence and the chief of staff of the TO." And then not highlighted but perhaps significant: "The minister of defence shall organise and supervise the Territorial Defence until the appointment of the commander."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this portion of the document, aside from recording the substantive step taken of designating and enacting commander of the Territorial Defence is interesting in that we see the wording changed here, and we'll see this in later documents, I believe, from this body. This seems to record directly a decision taken by the National Security Council and doesn't make any more reference to proposing something to the president. But here again, the National Security Council seems to be acting directly as an executive organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, are there any further questions to be put? We couldn't put them now because we have to stop, but are there any further questions in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one, but I'll put it after the break. We'll adjourn until a quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I think I had one question on the document under tab 120. Mr. Treanor, would you have any guidance for me how to understand the line which says that: "It was proposed that the Presidency adopt measures for the removal of the causes of the situation that has emerged." I'm wondering what that would mean, and I'm just asking you whether you could of any further guidance to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I hope so, Your Honour. This is a formulation which appears in some of the legislation and other documents about emergency situations.
