Unfortunately, I've just changed the materials in my binder, so I do not have the text of Article 81 of the Constitution of the Bosnian Serb Republic before me. It's possible that it also may contain such wording. But anyways, the idea is that in an emergency situation, a certain body, normally the Presidency of the given republic, for instance, assumes powers, including the powers of the Assembly, if the Assembly is unable to meet, due to the situation, and one of the most -- or the primary focus of the duties of that body exercising the emergency powers should be precisely to remove the conditions, the emergency conditions, that led to the state of affairs as it then exists, that is, an emergency state of affairs. In other words, the job of the given body, assuming emergency powers should not be to reform the educational system or something like that, but to deal with the emergency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me try to understand you correctly. So this removal of the causes is not, in whatever way, a reference to, for example, removal of persons, which, of course, the presence of persons could be the cause of a problem. I'm just trying to find out whether -- since sometimes we see that texts are not sometimes a bit vague, and this is vague as well. You know that in some offences consist of forcible removal of persons. This is not an indirect reference to such a situation, in your view, or would you have any reason --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This would certainly not be a reference to only something like that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear to me. Please, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Treanor, in connection with some of your remarks about the discussions at the 15 April National Security Council meeting, can we turn next to tab 121, the 15 April 1992 decision on immediate threat of war.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This decision reflects the discussion and the proposal that was made at the session we just considered, to declare an imminent threat of war, mobilise the Territorial Defence, et cetera. I would call the Court's attention to the fact that at the very beginning of the document, the very top of that page, that this decision is issued pursuant to Article 81 of the constitution. That is the article that confers emergency powers on the presidents of the republic. That article also requires that any actions that the president may take that are -- that ordinarily would be within the competence of the National Assembly, be subsequently confirmed by the National Assembly, and at the bottom of the document we will see that in fact this decision was confirmed by the Assembly at its next session, which was held on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next two items will be found at tabs 29 and 30 of the intercept binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just perhaps verify first, on 121, under number 2 it reads in English: "Mobilisation of Territorial Defence in the whole territory of Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina is hereby ordered." Is that literally what it says in the original, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the original, an abbreviation is used, SBiH, which has here been rendered as Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The first is a conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Tieger, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry. The first intercepted telephone conversation is a conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Garic, dated 12 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Is this ERN 03220859 on the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The date I have on that transcript is the 21st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's correct. That is the -- I'm sorry. That's my mistake. Thank you for catching that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the screen it says the 12th of April as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Dyslexic screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Garic is a local Territorial Defence commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see Mr. Krajisnik, who, to remind the Court, is, at this point, not only the president of the Assembly but also a member of the National Security Council, dealing directly with a Territorial Defence commander on the local situation, military situation, in his area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next document is found at intercept tab 30, and that's a telephone conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karisik. The clip begins on page 2 of the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could, before this gets going, identify Mr. Karisik, who, until the establishment of the Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs, was the deputy chief of the special police unit within the SRBiH Ministry of Internal Affairs, and at this point he is now the chief of the similar unit within the Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, here we see Mr. Krajisnik dealing with a prominent police commander, and trying to get information about the situation in Sarajevo. The reference to the river is the river that flows through the middle of Sarajevo. Vraca is on one of the hills above the river and was the site of the police school of the SRBiH and had been taken over by the Bosnian Serb MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could return now to the document binder at tab 122, where the Chamber will find the minutes of the meeting of the National Security Council on April 22nd, 1992. And as the document indicates, an extended meeting of the council for national security and the Government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are minutes from another session of the National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The first highlighted section, Mr. Treanor, is the second paragraph under the heading, "Strategic issues," which begins: "It was agreed Serb Republic of BH to maintain the positions that had been taken, especially in Sarajevo," and continues on to the bottom of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is indicative of the type of matters that the National Security Council dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The second highlighted portion begins at the bottom of page 2, with the designation of the paragraph, that is, paragraph 2, military commanding, and continues on to page 2, with the first sentence: "It was decided that the president of the Council for national security coordinate command over the Territorial Defence forces and over political Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. operations."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, here we see a decision which, from the minutes, appears to be strictly a decision of the National Security Council without any reference to making a proposal to the acting presidents. And this particular decision assigns particular responsibility, indeed very important responsibilities, over military and political affairs to the president of the National Security Council, who is, of course, Dr. Karadzic, and who signs these minutes, as I believe the previous minutes and the others we will see, as the president of the council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And also on page 2 there's a highlighted portion under the paragraph 4, conclusions and reports, and the highlighted portions are numbers 3 and 4, that is, that: "Ministers in the Ministry of the Interior and in the national defence submit daily reports on the situation in the field." And number 4: "That the Ministry of the Interior submit daily reports on the security situation in the territory of the Serb Republic of BH."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision by the National Security Council that it be kept informed on a daily basis by the two ministries mentioned of developments around the country. Now, the reference in paragraph 4 to the security situation, I take it, is a reference, since it is separate from paragraph 3, to getting a report from the National Security Service. I would also add at this point -- I'm not sure if we're going to move on, but these minutes, unlike the previous set of minutes we saw, do not reflect precisely who was at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move, then, to tab 123, a document entitled, "Excerpt from the instructions for the operation of Crisis Headquarters of Serb people in the municipalities." Again, Mr. Treanor, I think this is a document which will be dealt with in somewhat more detail by other witnesses, so if I could ask you to address this relatively briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, the first page of that document contains two highlights, aside from the heading of the document, the first found in the first paragraph, first enumerated paragraph: "Crisis Headquarters in conditions of war takes over all the prerogatives and functions of the municipal assemblies when they are not able to convene." And the second is found at enumerated paragraph 6: "The operation of the Crisis Headquarters is based on constitutional and legal provisions, also on the decisions of the Assembly, Presidency, and the Government of the Serb Republic Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reference here to "Crisis Headquarters" is a translation of the expression which previously I have rendered as "Crisis Staff." In particular, that is the phrase that is used in the 19 December instructions. Paragraph 1 here assigns to the Crisis Staff the type of emergency powers that the president of the republic, in the Bosnian Serb Republic, has under Article 81 of the constitution. This document exists in different versions which vary among themselves only very slightly. Apparently one copy was sent out prematurely, hadn't been quite finished, and the government sent out another copy on the 1st of May. That copy -- the copy that went out on the 1st -- apparently went out on the 1st of May continues to bear the date of 26th April, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn quickly to page 2. There are two highlights there, paragraphs 11 and 14, 11 addressing responsibility of Crisis Headquarters or Crisis Staffs for collecting information about the situation in the field and notifying and consulting the competent authorities," and number 14: "Crisis Headquarters make decisions and convene when all its members present, keeps official minutes, issues written instructions, and prepares weekly reports."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the desire for information through another chain, that is, from the Crisis Staffs. Mr. Djeric, who signed this document as the president of the government, is, of course, also a member of the National Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document selected by Mr. Treanor appears at tab 124.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That again is a meeting of the National Security Council and the Government of the Serbian Republic held on 28 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps at this point I can point out that these minutes do not bear a number of the session the way we've seen with the National Assembly, for instance, and I think we'll later see with the separate sessions of the government and the Presidency. Therefore, we are by no means certain that we have copies of all the minutes of meetings of the National Security Council that may have been created.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the record, one portion of that document is highlighted, and that is enumerated paragraph 9: "The reports on the works of Crisis Staffs and municipal organs of government were adopted." And then it continues to the remainder of that brief paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Reference is made to -- also to reports by Ostojic. The next name I decipher in the original as in fact being Subotic, who we just met as being the minister of defence and the acting commander of the Territorial Defence, and the reference to Ostojic is presumably to Velibor Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is contained in binder 12, which may or may not need to be distributed at this time. We're turning now to tab 125, behind which is found the decision on establishing penitentiary institutions.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And as the Court can see, this decision is also issued on the basis of Article 81 of the constitution, and it's as published in the gazette signed by the acting presidents who are here described as members of the Presidency. And it was later confirmed by the National Assembly at its session on the 12th of May. I call attention to Article 8 in particular. Now, I'm not an expert in criminal law or criminal procedure, but I think the reference here is to the fact that the -- what are here described as penitentiary re-education institutions are prisons in which people that have been through the judicial process serve their terms, as opposed to detention, which is a preliminary type of ordinarily pre-trial arrest, something of that nature. The minister of justice is given authority here. At this particular point in time, or shortly thereafter, Mr. Momcilo Mandic was named as minister of justice. As the Court may remember, we have come across him before as an assistant minister in the SRBiH Ministry of Internal Affairs. During the month of April, he was also, I believe, the deputy minister of the Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs but very soon became minister of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record, Mr. Treanor, you were referring to Article 8, which reads: "The minister of justice is hereby authorised to issue orders for the establishment of detention units within penitentiary re-education institutions."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could turn now again to the intercept binder, to tab 31. This is a conversation between Mr. Mandic and Mr. Ostojic. There are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, may I just ask you to stop, because of the speed, we now and then are a bit behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask a question. The title of the decision about the establishment of the penitentiary institutions. You indicated that there were detention facilities as well here. Are we talking about an issue of translation or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Article 8, in the English, there is reference to detention units, which I think is an adequate - again, without being a legal expert - an adequate rendering of the B/C/S expression that is used there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what we're talking about here is establishment of two types of institutions. Because the title of the decision is quite clear. These are penitentiary institutions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the title is clear, and I think one could put it that way, that in fact two different types of institutions are being established here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or at least authorisation for the establishment of a different -- of a second type of institution is being given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I would have a question to you as well. The abbreviation "KPO" is explained, for example, in Article 4, and we find the same in 5 and 6, as penitentiary re-education organisations. What exactly is the difference? Because in Article 8, we find penitentiary education institutions, just as we find that in the title of the decision. What exactly is the difference between a penitentiary and re-education organisation and a penitentiary and re-education institution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very good question, Your Honour. If we look at the title of this decision, it refers to penitentiary re-education -- let me just adopt that phrase. But in the original, in the title, it does use the word "organisation." In the beginning of Article 2, I can see the word "organisation" is used again. After that, we see an abbreviation being used, "KPO," "O" being for "organisation." In Article 8, on the other hand, if we can return to that, the word "organisation" is not used. The word "Dom" is used, Dom, which can be rendered as "house" or "home," house of detention, that sort of thing, in that sense. Now, in the SRBiH, that was the term used to designate these types of institutions. Apparently here they are changing the name slightly into penitentiary re-education organisations. I could only speculate that perhaps in Article 8 the drafter may have slipped up and used the old, more familiar term by mistake. But there is a different word used there, as opposed to the word used in the title of the decision and in other articles of the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Treanor. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we were about to listen to an intercepted telephone conversation involving Mr. Mandic and Mr. Stojic. There are two brief clips in that conversation, the first of which is contained at page 8 behind tab 31, and the second of which is found at page 9 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go to that particular intercept, just in relation to the last exchange between Your Honour and the witness, I wasn't sure if when the witness, Mr. Treanor, was referring to an inadequate or an adequate translation. I heard it as "inadequate," but it came across on the screen as "adequate." So I was just wondering if that could be cleared up before we proceeded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, did you consider it inadequate or an adequate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really can't remember using the term. If I could see the transcript. Is that the right button? Where are we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am afraid that we need now the assistance of those who can scroll back. Perhaps, Mr. Acquaviva, could you scroll back to adequate or inadequate or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please read the line in which the word "adequate" appears for which Ms. Loukas asks us whether it should be "inadequate." Could you also perhaps indicate on what page and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what line it appears.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's page 48, line 14. The witness states: "In Article 8, in the English, there is reference to detention units, which I think is an adequate - again, without being a legal expert - an adequate rendering of the B/C/S expression that is used there."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I said "adequate."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was the part you referred to, Ms. Loukas?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, Your Honour. It's just that I think, as I was hearing it, it was a bit difficult to determine whether it was "adequate" or "inadequate."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's good to see that the emergency measures really serve their purpose. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we can now proceed to play those two brief intercept clips. Again, since some time has transpired before we introduced those, I just want to identify the participants again, and that's Mr. Mandic and Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The date of this conversation being given as the 5th of May. I believe that Mr. Mandic by this time had been appointed minister of justice, but, as I mentioned previously, he had been an assistant minister in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Mr. Kvesic, who was a Bosnian Croat, had been the under-secretary for state security within that ministry. That made him basically the head of the State Security Service and also more or less a colleague of Mr. Mandic during the period when they both served in that ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you for identifying the -- that is a longish conversation, which begins, I believe, with Mr. Mandic and Mr. Kvesic, and then Mr. Stojic that participates, and I believe that's the part of the conversation which I believe the Court will hear.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Stojic was also an assistant minister in the Ministry of Internal Affairs, also a Bosnian Croat. Mr. Kvesic became, in the Herceg-Bosna, the Bosnian Croat entity, at a particular point in time, and I don't know whether that has occurred yet, the head of what was basically their Ministry of Internal Affairs, and Mr. Stojic became the head of what was basically their Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the next clip, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask you where exactly, on what page we found this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's on page 8, Your Honour. It begins in approximately the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was the clip we just played, and we're moving on to page 9, toward the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first clip is an indication of certainly Mr. Mandic's view on the state of relations with the Muslim side in the conflict, that is, they don't want to negotiate, so now they're not going to get anything. On the other hand, he seems to be interested in the second clip, and in the rest of this conversation, in exploring the possibility of an agreement with the Bosnian Croats, who have their centre in the Mostar area and in Western Herzegovina. Mr. Mandic raises, however, a claim by the Bosnian Serbs to basically having a border on the Neretva, which we've seen reference to before, and which Mr. Stojic seems to think is out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could turn back to binder 12, tab 126, behind which is a session of the National Security Council and the Government of the Serbian Republic, held on 10 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And on the front page of that record, Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted a portion of what appears under what is headed I, and states that: "The following agenda was proposed for the Assembly session," referring to the sentence above about the Assembly session to be held on 12 May 1992 in Banja Luka, and goes on to indicate: "Submission of reports, report on the political and war situation," and continues down to number 2: "Verification of decisions and other regulations within the competence of the Assembly adopted by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it goes on to specify other items which the Security Council proposes should be on the agenda for that session. Again, these minutes are not numbered, so we don't know which session of the National Security Council this was. I think we saw reference earlier in previous minutes to having daily meetings. We certainly do not have minutes for a meeting held every day. These minutes also, I can observe, are not signed by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, anything further before we move on to the assembly session of 12 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, other than perhaps remarking that here we can see reflected some of the aspects of Article 81 of the constitution, that is, the Presidency or, as we've seen in certain cases, the National Security Council itself, adopting decisions within the competence of the Assembly and now arranging to submit them to confirmation by the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 16th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina held on 12 May 1992 is found behind tab 127.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'm going to direct your attention to a few of the sections from that assembly session which you have highlighted, but before doing that, may I ask you to provide the Chamber with the context and backdrop to this session.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is the first session of the assembly taken -- that met after the proclamation of independence on the -- early on the 7th of April and the beginning of hostilities throughout the country. It's difficult to give a precise date for that, but certainly, as we've seen, an imminent state of war was declared on the 15th of April. And in the interval between the 15th session and this session, the acting presidents were issuing decisions within the competence of the Assembly. The Assembly at this point has a long agenda, as can be seen on page 1 here, encompassing the verification of the decisions issued by the acting presidents and other legislative matters, including amendments to the constitution of the republic and amendments to the constitutional law. And pursuant to those amendments, the election of members of a newly re-formed Presidency. Also, important decisions were taken in relation to forming an army of the republic. And one of the most important decisions here, which I think we will see later and much discussion of, was a decision on defining what we refer to as the strategic goals of the Serbian people. These goals reflected some of the discussion in previous sessions that we've seen already. I think we can move on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention, then, Mr. Treanor, to page 13 of the English translation, pages 7 and 8 of the B/C/S. I know there's a great deal of highlighting, but as you've indicated earlier, this section refers to the strategic goals and enumerates them.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a very important discussion on the strategic goals. This is Dr. Karadzic speaking. He indicates at the beginning of his remarks that these goals have been formulated by the Presidency, the government, and the National Security Council. And as we can see, the first such goal is separation from the other two national communities, separation of states.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that's the paragraph which begins: "The Serbian side in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Presidency, the government, the Council for National Security, which we have set up, have formulated the strategic priorities," and concludes: "Separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with such practices if we were to stay together in the same state."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you continue, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next paragraph contains discussion of the second goal, which is a corridor between Semberija and Krajina. The reference here to Semberija is to the north-eastern part of Bosnia and, and Krajina, of course, being in the western part of Bosnia. We saw mention of the -- what is at issue here in one of the documents from February, I think it was -- related to the meeting that took place in Doboj, the idea that there should be a link between those two areas along the Bosnian side of the Sava River, in order that the territory controlled by the Bosnian Serbs would be continuous and communication be possible from Eastern Bosnia, not only to Western Bosnia, but further on into the Republic of Serbian Krajina in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the second strategic goal is contained in the paragraph immediately following. I should note for the record that the strategic goals in order are separated by paragraphs and have been highlighted, or rather, the discussion of the strategic goals by Dr. Karadzic. Looking at the third paragraph, the third strategic goal, Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The next paragraph specifies as a third strategic goal the establishment of a corridor in the Drina Valley. Now, the Drina Valley, or the Drina, the River Drina, was, for much of its course, although not all of its course, the boundary between BH and Serbia. On the Bosnian side, the population was fairly heavily Muslim. And the valley also, in a certain respect, formed a link between north-eastern Bosnia, Semberija, which we saw reference to in the previous goal, and Eastern Herzegovina, which is a heavily Serbian area in south-eastern Bosnia. So the idea here is to eliminate a barrier, the Drina as a barrier, the Drina Valley as a barrier between Bosnia, or at least the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Serbia, on the one hand, and between two parts of the Serbian Republic itself, that is, between Semberija in the north-east and Eastern Herzegovina in the south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move on to the fourth strategic goal contained in the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth goal refers to the establishment of a border on the rivers Una and Neretva. Now, those two rivers are in different parts of the country. The Una is in the far north-western part of Bosnia, and the municipality of Bosanska Krupa is on that river. We've seen some mention made of that municipality several times in Assembly sessions. That municipality was basically bisected by the Una river. And the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa was formed on the east bank of the river, and therefore, among other -- and the other side of the river was very heavily populated by Muslims, and the Bosnian Serbs were content to leave that area to the Bosnian Muslims, hence the reference here to a border on the Una, which is a rather short stretch, by the way. And then we see the reference to a border on the Neretva. Now, the Neretva flows to the sea from just south of Sarajevo. It's fairly lengthy. And the territory on the east bank, which the Bosnian Serbs here would be proclaiming -- claiming, was also claimed by not only the Muslims but by the Bosnian Croats, as we saw in the previous conversation on the telephone between Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Mandic and Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, Dr. Karadzic discusses the fifth strategic goal.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fifth goal, as the Court can see, relates to Sarajevo and dividing the city into Serbian and Muslim parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, for the record, the highlighted portion continues onto the beginning portions of page 14, ending with the sentence: "In addition, the fighting in Sarajevo keeps the fighting far away from Krajina, far away from Semberija, far away from the Drina, far away from all those areas where we could possibly have conflicts with Muslims." And I believe the next paragraph addresses the sixth strategic goal. The first sentence of that next paragraph is highlighted: "The sixth strategic goal is the access of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the sea. It is not unimportant."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Access to the sea had also come up in some of the discussion in previous Assembly sessions. I can only point out that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had access to the sea, a very small stretch of the coast which was deliberately given to it for that purpose. Otherwise, the boundary between Bosnia, or at that point, Herzegovina, and Croatia is formed by the mountains which come very close to the sea. The small portion of the coast that was given to Bosnia is in a Croatian-inhabited part of the country. And if my geography is correct, it is on the western side of the Neretva River. So precisely how access to the sea could be realised without coming into rather serious conflict with not only the Bosnian Croats but the Republic of Croatia, is very difficult to see, since the coast itself is, even in the portion that is in Bosnia, as I mentioned, is inhabited basically by Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn now to some of the other portions of the 16th Assembly Session, which you've highlighted. First if we could turn to page 16 of the English, pages 10 and 11 of the B/C/S, remarks by Mr. Beli. Immediately following the identification of him as a speaker, you've highlighted what appear to be his first three sentences, indicating he'd like to make a few remarks on the: "Priority tasks set by our president. One of the first priorities is establishing communication between Semberija and the Bosnian Krajina, and since Brcko is practically in the centre of all these events, I must inform you that the operations to establish this communication have been completed, to a degree, in the military aspect." And then you've highlighted another sentence a short time later in his remarks, in which he states: "However, for definitive clearing of the area, it will be necessary to have many more forces there, and, first of all, we will undoubtedly need help to maintain the current situation."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would just remark that Dr. Beli is a nickname for Mr. Vojinovic who is a deputy. He was elected to the Chamber of Citizens, and he is from Brcko. Therefore, the Brcko area is naturally very important to him, and the idea of the corridor, which has been specified as one of the strategic goals, is very important to him. Brcko is a key location along that corridor. It's on the River Sava itself. And he's calling attention here to the situation there and the fact that they're going to need help there, which means help keeping that corridor open.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And turning to a later portion of Dr. Beli's speech, found on page 17 of the English and page 11 of the B/C/S. The portion highlighted is: "So I would ask President Karadzic and President Krajisnik, because they can communicate with the Serbian people through the media, to promote this more, and I must say that the Serbian people, especially in parts like Brcko, where we are 20 per cent, and as you have been saying, Mr. President, the Serbs are not a conquering people and do not get involved easily in these conquests that are currently necessary."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we have an appeal for help in that area, which, as Mr. Vojinovic points out, is a Serbian-minority area, but nevertheless is very strategically important for the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn next to page 24 of the English, page 16 of the B/C/S. You've highlighted some remarks by Mr. Vjestica. The highlighted portion appear toward the bottom of the page: "On the right bank of the Una River there are no more Muslims in the Serbian Municipality of Bosanska Krupa. All the enclaves that were there, Rapusa, Veliki Vrbovik, Ostroznica, Babic, Muslim Jasenica and Zavir we have evacuated them so that there will be none there for the duration of the war operations." And then it ends with the sentence: "Will they have a place to return to? I think it is unlikely after our president told us the happy news that the right bank of the [sic] is the border."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reference to the right bank is, of course, to the right bank of the Una. That is the eastern bank the river. Mr. Vjestica is a deputy and is from Bosanska Krupa. Therefore, the situation there is uppermost in his mind. I think we've seen him speak before, and here he's assuring deputies that basically that the border on the Una, which is one of the goals, has been secured in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, you referred earlier to some of the important events that took place at the 16th Assembly Session. You've just discussed the enunciation of the strategic goals. Was the army also established on that date and was a commander for the army selected?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of the important decisions taken was to form an army. When the constitution and the defence law were first adopted on the 28th of February, it was foreseen that the Republic would be within the framework of Yugoslavia. Dr. Karadzic referred to that later on, as we've seen, that the JNA would be their army, but that, like other republics within Yugoslavia, they would have a Territorial Defence. Now that they have -- now that the Assembly has declared independence at the beginning of April, they need a new defence set-up. So at this point, they decide to form an army and appoint a military commander for that army, namely, General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we turn to some retrospective remarks from it Dr. Karadzic from the 50th Session of the Serbian Assembly held in April 1995 and found behind tab 128, does he indicate who selected General Mladic as commander of the army? And I direct the Court and counsel's attention to B/C/S page 176 and 177, and English translation 146.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This indicates that Dr. Karadzic was directly involved in the identification and selection of General Mladic for the position to which the Assembly appointed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And have you highlighted the portion of the -- of that Assembly session which begins: "Gentlemen, we got the officers we asked for." Continues: "I asked for Mladic." Indicates that he had noticed Mladic's blunt statements in the newspapers. He took -- Dr. Karadzic took an interest in him, and together with Mr. Krajisnik, went to General Kukanjac's office and listened to him issuing orders and commanding around Kupres and Knin. "We spent countless nights in the office of General Kukanjac at that time." Then he indicates that President Krajisnik was already president of the Assembly, although Dr. Karadzic was just president of the party and had no state function and concludes with the sentence: "We asked for Mladic and said that they should set up the headquarters as they saw fit. We wouldn't interfere."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I would just observe that, to clarify what's going on here, General Kukanjac was the commander of the 2nd Military District in Sarajevo, and I'm not sure precisely when, toward the end of April or the beginning of May 1992, General Mladic, who had been the commander of the JNA corps headquartered in Knin, in Croatia, was appointed to be the -- I'm not sure whether it was the deputy commander or the chief of staff of the 2nd Military District. So the reference is apparently to the fact that General Mladic was present on the scene in Sarajevo shortly before this session on the 12th of May, so that Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik had an opportunity to observe him in action, so to speak, directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one question in that respect. That's the following: We do not have the complete tape-recording. We have page 1, and then it continues on page 144. I'm not going to ask you for 142 pages, but I'd just like to know whether anything changed in the presence of those who attended this session. Because on the first page it says that Momcilo Krajisnik opened the session. But of course, I cannot check whether he left the meeting in between. Was he -- is there any indication in the minutes or in the tape-recording that he would have left the meeting up until the moment when these words were spoken by Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, Your Honour, but I can certainly double-check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If your answer would be different, we'd like to know, either today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could return to page -- excuse me, to tab 127.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I could direct Mr. Treanor's attention to page 32 of the B/C/S and page 49 of the English -- I'm sorry. Page 37 of the B/C/S and page 49 of the English. You've highlighted some remarks by Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here Mr. Krajisnik addresses the -- what he calls the war option and the strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The first highlighted portion begins in the second paragraph, after he's identified as the speaker on that page, and states: "In reality, if we are establishing an army, it means that we do expect the war option." It continues: "It would not look good if the conclusion of the Assembly would be that we have chosen the option of war. The option of war is the choice of those who want to occupy something that does not belong to them. Although in my heart I believe that Mr. Kalinic is right, because we will surely go to war." And the second highlighted portion is found further down on that page and reads: "As for the goals, I would just like to offer an explanation, since I have also taken part in adopting these goals," and continues: "Have we finally --" it continues on through another couple of sentences, ending: "Have we finally decided to separate from the remaining two national communities? We can part from them if Bosnia and Herzegovina is to be torn into three parts."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is certainly an interesting commentary on Mr. Krajisnik's participation in the formulation of the goals, and I would also observe, to help clarify the first extract, that Mr. Kalinic, who is referred to, who we may have come across earlier, was, I believe, in fact, a doctor. He was an independent deputy in the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina before the outbreak of hostilities, but he joined the Assembly of the Serbian People either at its formation or very shortly thereafter. And at about this time - I don't know the precise date - he was named by the Assembly to be the minister of health of the Bosnian Serb Republic. It was possible, under the constitution, for a deputy to be a minister without losing the deputies' -- their deputies' mandate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we can turn to page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 50 of the English translation, page 34 of the B/C/S. Mr. Krajisnik's remarks continue, and there are two highlights on this page, the first of which is: "For us, there must be only one pleasure: To liberate our people for all time." And the second of which begins: "This about proclaiming a state of war, I think that it should be, if the Government of Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we shall probably proclaim it, but it is obvious that we must" -- and it continues on to the next page -- "not believe that we are only playing at war. We are at war, and it will be possible to solve this thing with Muslims and Croats only by war. And the politics will be instrumental in bringing it to an end." And one more portion highlighted in that page, which begins: "Please, if we acquire the territories which we agree on and have conceived of today, plus the corridor we get up there, we will have done, this generation will have done so much for the Serbian people." And then it continues to the last sentence of that highlighted portion: "That is what I would like to ask you: Can we adopt this bulletin?" I believe those are your highlights number 34 and 35, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have anything to add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention, then, to tab 131, the decision -- well, maybe move first to tab 130. Excuse me. Mr. Treanor, shown here and contained behind tab 30 is the decision on strategic objectives of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I take it that is the version that was published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And as the Court will observe, it was not published until November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The decision on establishing the army is contained behind tab 131. Can we direct our attention to that, please, Mr. Treanor. And it is presently shown on screen.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have the decision on the army, indeed, as published in the Official Gazette at the time, later on, in May. And as the Court can see, in Article 3, General Ratko Mladic is appointed commander of the Main Staff of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: May I next direct your attention to the next document you've selected, which is found at tab 132, the decision on promulgating the law amending the constitution.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is actually the law on amending the constitutional law. I call attention to Article 1, beginning in paragraph 2. If we could magnify that. In paragraph 2 of Article 1. Now, this specifies that instead of the two acting presidents fulfilling the function of the President of the Republic, the Assembly would now elect a three-member Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that you were referring to Article 1 of this law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In which it says that paragraph 2 of Article 5 of the Law on the Constitution is changed? Because I do not find any paragraph 2 in Article 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The paragraphs are not numbered. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. If I could direct your attention to page 3. I thought there was a highlighted section there. There is not. But -- so I'll move on to the decision proclaiming amendments to the constitution, unless you have additional comments.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A further provision in that Article 1 is that the three-member Presidency would select from its number a president of the Presidency, and further specifies that the Presidency would adopt rules of procedure for its work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think I have time to move you on to one further document, contained at tab 135. That's the decision proclaiming amendments to the constitution. Mr. Treanor, any comments on that document before we adjourn for the day?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a package of amendments that has to do with national defence, in particular, with the fact that an army has now been created. The constitution is being amended appropriately. And we see, in particular, in Amendment 3, which specifies that: "The army will be commanded by the President of the Republic in times of peace and during war, and that the President of the Republic shall appoint, promote, and discharge officers of the army."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger. First of all, I would like to ask you one question, but perhaps we could first escort Mr. Treanor out of the courtroom, accompanied by the same instructions I gave you the previous days, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I'd like to ask you the following: If we would also sit tomorrow in the afternoon - of course, a lot of preparations have to be made - the sooner we would know it, the better it will be. So if you have already an idea on whether, of course, apart from unforeseen problems, as we faced today, whether you'd need time in the afternoon tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you also think that if we would, well, let's say, start, for example, at 3.30 in the afternoon, and if the interpreters would be there, and if we could continue, well, let's say, for another two hours or two and a half or three hours, because it's never any further than 7.00, would we be able to finish tomorrow, you would think?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's obviously a more difficult question. I would be hopeful and optimistic about that. And as I indicated to you before, I would certainly aim toward that. I want to be candid and indicate it's hard to predict, but I think that is at least a realistic objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then a last minor issue. On tab 135, where we are at this moment, I see that, at least in Amendment 1, a part is not legible. I also see that in the original set, we also have a French translation, and the French translator seems to have no problems in reading what the English translator couldn't read. If you would clarify that before tomorrow, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. If I may, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify a couple of issues raised yesterday, very quickly. With respect to intercept binder tab 27, we have replaced the document, which now renders the pagination completely synchronised and accurate. We have replaced the B/C/S in tab 88. In tab 95, the material that was in Sanction that was not in the binder is now there. We have also replaced the pages that -- or provided the pages that Judge El Mahdi did not have yesterday. And we have provided the attachment which was the introductory speech to tab 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good to see that we have such a quick response from the Prosecution. Thank you, Mr. Tieger, for that. If there's nothing else to be raised, we'll adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of February, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
